## Three features in one file

Look at a classic raster VRT from GDAL and it's easy to see three
features sharing one XML file:

1. **Indirection.** The file holds references, not data. Reads go to
   other files, other locations, or several datasets presented as one.
2. **Metadata edits.** Attributes such as names, descriptions and labels
   are changed without touching the arrays.
3. **Operation chains.** Interpolation, regridding and the like are
   recorded as a lazy graph that runs when the data is read.

On this view, VRT bundles three jobs, and a modern stack would give each
one its own home: references in a virtual Zarr store, attributes in its
metadata, and the graph in a lazy engine.

As an inventory of what can appear in a VRT, that is fair. As an account
of why VRT works, and why newer tools keep arriving at parts of it but
never the whole, it misses most of the design. The three features describe what goes *in* the
file. The design is in what the file *is* and how it *behaves*. Read that
way, VRT is six properties, and they cut across the three features:

| Property | In one line |
|---|---|
| **Closure** | the result is a dataset, so it opens anywhere and composes |
| **Names** | sources are dataset names, from any driver, through any I/O chain |
| **Placement** | windows of sources are pasted into windows of the output, aligned or not |
| **Assertion** | the VRT augments a source, supplying what it lacks and correcting what it gets wrong |
| **Deferral** | nothing is read until a window is requested |
| **Emission** | tools write it; almost no large VRT is written by hand |

## Where the boundary sits

"VRT" covers several things that share a name. This post is about
**classic raster VRT**: a `<VRTDataset>` of `<VRTRasterBand>` elements fed
by sources (Simple, Complex, Averaged, KernelFiltered), plus derived bands
and warped VRTs. The full grammar is in
[`gdalvrt.xsd`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OSGeo/gdal/master/frmts/vrt/data/gdalvrt.xsd).
The neighbours appear only to show where classic ends:

- **`vrt://` strings**: one source dataset with `gdal_translate` options
  written as a URI, so there is no file.
- **Multidimensional VRT**: groups, dimensions and arrays. Sources are
  placed by index slabs, and derived arrays add View, Transpose, Resample
  and Grid steps.
- **Vector VRT** (`OGRVRTDataSource`): layers built from other layers,
  with fields, geometry from columns, SQL, regions and unions.
- **GTI** (sources as rows of a vector layer) and **GDALG** (a saved
  `gdal` pipeline that opens as a dataset): close relatives, not VRT.

The six properties do not divide neatly between classic and the rest. All
six are present in classic raster VRT. What changes from family to family
is how strongly each one shows.

## Closure

A VRT is a dataset. It opens wherever GDAL opens a dataset, every GDAL
tool reads it, and it can be the source of another VRT. That one fact is
what "serialised in one go to an XML file" is really doing. It is not a
packaging detail; it is why VRT composes. A SQL view has the same idea.

- **Classic raster:** full. A source can be another `.vrt`, by path or
  through any `/vsi` chain, or a `vrt://` string, and the nesting goes as
  deep as you like.
- **Beyond classic:** every family is closed in its own model. The
  exception is that `vrt://` strings cannot nest, because GDAL splits the
  string at the first `?`. GDALG brings closure to whole pipelines.

## Names

A source is a dataset name, not a file path. It can be any driver
(`NETCDF:"f.nc":sst`), any `/vsi` chain
(`/vsizip/{/vsicurl/https://host/a.zip}/b.tif`), any subdataset, or another
VRT. Anything GDAL can open can be placed. A name can even cross data
models: `vrt://f.zarr?transpose=/sst:1,2` picks two dimensions of a
multidimensional array to form a classic raster, with the rest as bands,
and that string can sit in `SourceFilename` like any other. That reach is
where the "indirection" of the three-feature view really lives. VRT redirects to
*datasets*, not to bytes.

- **Classic raster:** full, through `SourceFilename` and its
  `relativeToVRT` attribute.
- **Beyond classic:** the same names are used in every family (vector adds
  open options beside the name). No family's schema types the name; in
  `gdalvrt.xsd`, `SourceFilename` is a plain `xs:string`. What a name
  means is defined by the drivers' open code, which is why names are the
  hardest part to carry outside GDAL.

## Placement

A window of a source is pasted into a window of the output. Offsets can be
fractional, sizes can differ, and sources can overlap. When a request
arrives, GDAL works out which source window feeds which output window and
resamples where the sizes or offsets require it. This is the second half
of "indirection" (several datasets as one), and no system outside GDAL
has it.

- **Classic raster:** this is classic's home ground. `SrcRect` and
  `DstRect` are arbitrary 2D windows, and every `ComplexSource` can carry
  its own resampling.
- **Beyond classic:** multidimensional VRT places sources by integer
  slabs (`SourceSlab`, `DestSlab`), with no resampling inside a source;
  resampling is a separate derived step. A `vrt://` string places one
  window (`srcwin`, `projwin`, `outsize`). Vector VRT has no placement in
  this sense: its nearest equivalents are clipping to a region and
  stacking layers in a union.

GTI exists because classic VRT stops scaling here. Every source is listed
in the XML, so opening a VRT parses every source entry, and nothing
indexes them in space. GTI keeps placement and moves the sources into rows
of an indexed vector layer.

Placement is also where the three-feature split breaks down. In real
mosaics, indirection *is* an operation:

- **USGS 3DEP 1 arc-second seamless VRT** (3,817 tiles, read 2026-11-05):
  every tile is placed at a fractional offset and read with bilinear
  resampling. The VRT writes its pixel size as 2.777778e-4 degree, while
  the tiles sit on a 1/3600-degree pitch, so the tile offsets drift by up
  to 0.10 px across the mosaic. The "redirection" becomes an interpolation
  on every read, caused by one rounded constant. The tiles also overlap
  their neighbours by 6 pixels.
- **Copernicus DEM GLO-30 as one VRT** (26,475 tiles): 55 % of the tiles
  are resampled to the common grid, because their native widths change
  with latitude. Every one of the remaining 45 % overlaps a neighbour by a
  pixel.

A virtual Zarr store (kerchunk, VirtualiZarr, Icechunk) can hold none of
these placements. It references chunks that line up exactly with its own
grid. By contrast, the GHRSST MUR daily COGs as a multidimensional VRT
(38,360 placements across five arrays) are all aligned, identity
placements. For data shaped like that, the VRT and a byte-reference store
carry the same information, and the three-feature split works.

## Assertion

The VRT augments a source, supplying what it lacks and correcting what it
gets wrong, without copying a byte. The assertions that matter change what the bytes *mean*: a CRS for a file
that has none, a corrected geotransform, a nodata value, a scale and
offset. Seven of the 29 keys of the `vrt://` syntax begin with `a_` for
"assign" (`a_srs`, `a_ullr`, `a_gt`, `a_nodata`, `a_scale`, `a_offset`,
`a_coord_epoch`). Metadata repair is one of the main reasons people write
VRTs at all.

- **Classic raster:** `SRS`, `GeoTransform`, `NoDataValue`, `Offset`,
  `Scale`, `ColorInterp`, band `Description` and metadata. Renaming barely
  applies, because classic bands are numbered and a description is all
  they have.
- **Beyond classic:** renaming is real in the other families. Arrays and
  dimensions are named in multidimensional VRT, and fields are renamed and
  retyped in vector VRT. Multidimensional VRT can also assert whole
  coordinates (`RegularlySpacedValues`) and dimension types. Vector VRT
  asserts geometry type, layer CRS and geometry built from columns.

The 3DEP case shows why assertion belongs next to placement. An exact
pixel size of 1/3600 degree would make every one of its placements
integer, and remove the resampling entirely.

## Deferral

Opening a VRT plans; it does not read. Ask for a window, and GDAL works
out which sources, which source windows and which operations that window
needs before it touches a byte. So a VRT is cheap to make, cheap to pass
on, and cheap to throw away.

- **Classic raster:** full. Each read runs the source-to-output window
  calculation for the requested window, and GDAL's block cache sits
  underneath.
- **Beyond classic:** the same in every family. The plan, though, lives
  only inside GDAL's objects. No family exposes it as data that another
  process, language or engine could take.

## Emission

Tools compile *to* VRT. That is how VRTs with thousands of sources exist,
and it means replacing VRT requires replacing what writes it, not only
what reads it.

- **Classic raster:** written by `gdalbuildvrt`, `gdal_translate -of VRT`,
  `gdalwarp -of VRT`, and `gdal raster mosaic` and `stack`. Most classic
  VRTs in the wild are tool output.
- **Beyond classic:** `gdal mdim mosaic` (GDAL 3.12) and
  `gdalmdimtranslate -of VRT` write multidimensional VRT. Vector VRTs are
  mostly written by hand or by scripts. `vrt://` strings are written by
  people and by packages that build dataset names. GDALG is written by
  `gdal` pipelines.

## Operations come from placement and assertion

The third feature of the three-feature view is real, but it is not a
property of its own. It is what placement and assertion become once they
compute values.

- **Classic raster:** derived bands with pixel functions, warped VRTs,
  and the per-source operations of `ComplexSource` (scale, offset, LUT,
  nodata), `KernelFilteredSource` and `AveragedSource`. The most common
  operation in practice is the one hidden inside placement: a resample
  whenever a source window and output window differ.
- **Beyond classic:** derived arrays in multidimensional VRT, SQL and
  reprojected layers in vector VRT, and whole pipelines in GDALG.

## The boundary in one table

| | Classic raster | `vrt://` | Multidimensional | Vector |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Closure | full, nests | one level only | full | full |
| Names | full | the string is a name | full | full, plus open options |
| Placement | arbitrary 2D windows, resampled per source | one window | integer slabs; resampling is a derived step | none; regions and unions |
| Assertion | CRS, geotransform, nodata, scale, offset | the seven `a_` keys | plus coordinates, dimension types, names | geometry, CRS, field names and types |
| Deferral | full | full | full | full |
| Emission | many GDAL tools | people and packages | `gdal mdim mosaic`, `gdalmdimtranslate` | mostly by hand |
| Operations | pixel functions, warped VRT, per-source ops | translate options | derived array steps | SQL, reprojection |

Classic raster VRT is the strongest form of placement and emission. It is
the reason "VRT" means a mosaic to most people, and it is the family the
three-feature view was drawn from. It is also where that view goes wrong:
each feature can be pointed to in the XML, but in placement, indirection
and computation are one thing.

## Each property turns up elsewhere

| Turns up as | Where |
|---|---|
| byte-level references, plus history | kerchunk, VirtualiZarr, Icechunk |
| sources as rows with statistics, so planning becomes pruning | Iceberg, Delta, Lance; GDAL's own GTI |
| the plan as a value an engine optimises | Polars, DuckDB, DataFusion, JAX |
| assertion as declared metadata | Zarr v3 attributes and conventions |
| saved operation chains that reopen | `gdal` pipelines and `.gdalg.json` |
| memory shared across languages and processes | Arrow, mizu |

Each of these does its part better than VRT does. None does all six, and
outside GDAL none composes misaligned windows of arbitrary formats by
name. Inside GDAL that is classic raster VRT, and GTI as its answer to
scale.

## What a replacement has to keep

Splitting VRT into parts is the right instinct for an ecosystem that wants
each part done well in its own place. The six properties add two cautions.

1. **The split is exact only for aligned data.** For model output stored
   one file per step, a VRT lowers to byte references with nothing lost.
   For imagery mosaics, placement *is* an operation, so indirection and
   regridding have to be modelled together. A converter from VRT to
   virtual Zarr should say, source by source, which placements become byte
   references exactly and why the rest cannot.
2. **A replacement has to keep closure, deferral and emission.** Without
   them, it replaces the file format but not what made the format useful:
   a dataset that opens anywhere, plans before it reads, and is written by
   the tools people already run.

*The counts above come from reading each VRT's XML, with no source opened.
The 3DEP and GHRSST VRTs were read on 2026-11-05, and the COP30 source
table on 2026-10-19. The script and results are in
[wxylib/design, measurements/m29-vrt-rework](https://github.com/wxylib/design/tree/main/measurements/m29-vrt-rework).*
